summary:
For centuries, Andean farmers read the stars, winds, and clouds to guide their harvests. Today, accelerating climate change has broken those natural cycles: erratic rainfall, sudden droughts, and shifting frosts have stripped ancestral knowledge of the certainty it once held, putting family livelihoods and food security at risk.

Musuq Allpa crosses 20 complete years of daily NASA climate data (2006–2025) over the farmer's exact parcel with documented physiological requirements for 38 Peruvian crops (FAO EcoCrop) and 9 agronomic rotation rules. In ~200 milliseconds directly in the browser, it tells the farmer what crops are viable for the upcoming season and how to chain the next three agricultural campaigns; backing every recommendation with its exact data point, source, formula, and known limitation.
details:
1. THE VISION: COMPLEMENTING ANCESTRAL WISDOM WITH NASA DATA

For generations, Peruvian farmers relied on ancestral knowledge of the land and sky to plan their harvests. Today, climate variability has disrupted historical rainfall patterns and frost seasons, stripping farmers of the certainty they once had. At the same time, scientific satellite portals are too complex for daily field use, and coarse 50 km climate grids misrepresent local mountain microclimates.

Musuq Allpa ("New Land" in Quechua) bridges this gap. It is a fast, accessible web application that crosses 20 years of daily NASA satellite climate data (2006–2025) over the farmer's parcel with the biological requirements of 38 Peruvian crops (FAO EcoCrop) and 9 agronomic rotation rules (sourced from FAO, the International Potato Center - CIP, and traditional Andean practices). Instead of replacing the farmer, it listens to their field experience to recommend what to plant next and how to plan the following three agricultural campaigns.

2. HOW IT WORKS

Musuq Allpa operates through a clean, step-by-step workflow that runs in ~200 milliseconds directly in the user's phone or browser:

2.1. Listening to the Farmer & the Land: The farmer selects their location (via GPS or district list) and answers 4 simple questions: what they planted in recent seasons, what water access they have (rainfed, regular irrigation, or seasonal irrigation), what they want to prioritize (soil health, water efficiency, climate resilience, or diversification), and what they observe in their soil.

2.2. Solving the "Mountain Altitude Blind Spot": NASA POWER climate cells (~50 km wide) average deep agricultural valleys with freezing mountain peaks. Our engine compares the satellite cell's elevation against the parcel's true elevation and applies a standard vertical lapse-rate correction (-6.5 °C per km). In Huamancaca (3,186 m vs. the 3,770 m satellite cell), this corrects a +3.8 °C cold bias before evaluating crops.

*Graphic made with AI

2.3. Simulating 20 Years of Crop Windows: For each crop and every possible planting month, the engine tests the crop's exact growth cycle (e.g., 155 days) across the last 20 historical campaigns using daily NASA POWER temperature, rainfall, and solar radiation data.

2.4. Clear Historical Frequencies: Instead of confusing star ratings or arbitrary success percentages, Musuq Allpa counts real historical events: for example, "in 3 of 19 campaigns rainfall did not reach the minimum" or "in 0 of 19 campaigns temperatures dropped below lethal frost limits." Water availability adjusts these rules dynamically, a rainfall deficit discards a crop under rainfed conditions, but becomes a simple advisory note if the farmer has regular irrigation.

2.5. Evaluating Crop Suitability & Rotation Rules: Viable crops are ranked using FAO EcoCrop's suitability model and checked against 9 agronomic succession rules; such as avoiding consecutive plantings of the same botanical family, spacing Solanaceae crops by at least two seasons, and rotating legumes after soil-depleting harvests.

2.6. Three 3-Season Rotation Strategies (A, B, and C):

- Strategy A (Current Practice): Projects the farmer's existing planting pattern over three seasons to make potential soil or climate risks visible.

- Strategy B (Soil & Diversification): Prioritizes crop family rotation and legume integration to protect long-term soil health.

- Strategy C (Climate & Water Resilience): Prioritizes hardy crops and optimal planting windows with the lowest historical frost, heat, and drought exposure.

The system orders and highlights the strategy that best matches the farmer's stated priority, and every single card includes a "¿Qué datos utilizamos?" (What data did we use?) section showing the exact NASA variable, period, value, and limitation.

3. REAL-WORLD VALIDATION ACROSS PERU'S DIVERSE REGIONS

We validated Musuq Allpa across four contrasting Peruvian agro-ecosystems using real NASA POWER series:

• Andean Valley – Huamancaca, Junín (3,186 m | Previous crop: Potato | Rainfed): After correcting the +3.8 °C satellite altitude bias, barley, quinoa, oats, and lentil emerge as compatible. Repeating potato triggers two Solanaceae rotation warnings; Strategy B proposes rotating: Potato → Lentil → Barley → Quinoa.

• Amazon Rainforest – Puerto Maldonado (186 m | Previous crop: Cassava | Rainfed): With 2,191 mm of annual rain and zero frost days in 20 years, highland crops are discarded due to heat stress; Strategy B proposes: Cassava → Cowpea → Kiwicha → Common Bean.

• High Altiplano – Puno (3,827 m) & Arid Coast – Chancay (44 m): Validated for extreme high-altitude frost resistance and coastal irrigation regimes.

4. WHY OUR APPROACH IS DIFFERENT & RELIABLE

• 100% Deterministic & Reproducible (No Runtime AI Hallucinations): All agronomic recommendations come from verifiable math and peer-reviewed thresholds, backed by 43 automated tests ensuring the same parcel and inputs always yield the exact same scientific result.

• Honest About Scientific Uncertainty: The app openly informs the user that NASA POWER cells cover ~50 km, that rainfall comes from satellite reanalysis (MERRA-2) rather than local rain gauges, that EcoCrop evaluates species rather than local seed varieties, and that NASA CMIP6 climate projections currently return no coverage (-999) for Peru—choosing transparency over simulated guesses.

• Accessible Everywhere: Built as a lightweight, zero-backend web application that downloads 20 years of daily NASA data in ~2 seconds and caches it locally on the farmer's phone for offline resilience.

5. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & DATA SOURCES

• Frontend & Core Engine: HTML5, CSS3, and modular Vanilla JavaScript (zero external dependencies; runs identically in mobile browsers and Node.js for automated testing).

• NASA Datasets:

- NASA POWER Daily API (Agroclimatology Community): 20-year daily historical series (2006–2025) for mean, maximum, and minimum temperatures (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN), bias-corrected MERRA-2 precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), and CERES solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN).

- NASA POWER Monthly Climate Projection API (NEX-GDDP-CMIP6): Integrated to verify coverage and transparently report data availability.

• Partner & Agronomic Databases:

- FAO EcoCrop Database: Physiological thresholds, cycle lengths, and lethal temperatures for 38 Peruvian crops.

- Agronomic Rotation Catalog: 9 documented crop succession rules based on FAO, CIP (International Potato Center), and Andean agricultural literature.

- Open-Meteo Elevation API & Browser Geolocation API.

6. USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE / SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

In full compliance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, our team declares the transparent use of AI/SI tools exclusively during the development and documentation phases:

• Visual Design & Image Creation (Google Gemini – Gemini 2.5 Pro & Imagen 3): Used to generate the Musuq Allpa project logo, UI mockups, and the explanatory workflow/altitude-correction infographic diagrams shown in this project page. All AI-generated visuals are explicitly identified here in the descriptive text, preserve their generation watermarks/metadata, and strictly exclude any official NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers.

• Coding, Debugging & Troubleshooting (Anthropic Claude – Claude Haiku 5.5): Used as a development assistant for JavaScript debugging, code troubleshooting, and verifying edge cases in our unit test suite.

• Documentation (Google Gemini – Gemini 2.5 Pro): Used to help translate, structure, and refine the English project documentation.

Note on Runtime Execution: Musuq Allpa uses ZERO AI or Large Language Models at runtime. Every agroclimatic calculation, altitude lapse-rate correction, historical frequency count, and crop rotation strategy is 100% deterministic, rule-based, and reproducible directly from NASA POWER and FAO EcoCrop datasets.
